abstract: Streaming speech-to-speech translation requires timely decisions about when partial input is sufficient for accurate translation. We present S3-S2ST, a model that learns to translate and speak from semantically aligned streaming supervision. By converting utterance-level speech pairs into incremental training examples, we teach a learned policy when to commit translations. Its adjustable threshold controls the quality--latency tradeoff on a fixed 640\,ms input grid. S3-S2ST delivers competitive English--Chinese translation on FLEURS and leads the evaluated streaming systems in translation quality on the internal 9-pair test set. On RealSI, adapting the threshold to buffered speech further improves quality over a low fixed threshold with little change in first-audio latency. We plan to release the model and code.

oneSentenceThesis: S3-S2ST 把整句语音对翻译成按语义切分的增量训练轨迹，用 640 ms 固定分块和可调 READ/WRITE 门限实现流式语音到语音翻译，在 FLEURS 和内部 9 对数据上验证了翻译质量，并在 RealSI 上展示了质量与延迟的权衡。
originalTitle: S3-S2ST: Semantically Supervised Streaming Speech-to-Speech Translation
